info.name: The Courier Guy API
info.description:
# **Welcome to the The Courier Guy API!**

Our REST API provides predictable, resource-oriented URLs, uses standard HTTP methods, and returns JSON-encoded responses with conventional HTTP status codes. It’s designed to be intuitive, reliable, and easy to integrate with modern systems.

Please use the API responsibly and within the boundaries of The Courier Guy’s [acceptable use policy](https://thecourierguy.co.za/aup/AUPolicy.pdf). This means accessing only resources and data that you are authorised to view, using endpoints as intended, and avoiding excessive or automated requests that could impact service stability or other users. Continued use of the API implies acceptance of these terms and responsible usage practices.

item.name: Authentication
item.description:
We use Bearer Token authentication for our API. To authenticate, simply include your token in the header of each request, like so:

"Authorization": "Bearer a601d99c75fc4c64b5a64288f97d52b4"

You can explore and test our API in a dedicated sandbox environment called **Sandbox Couriers**.

To get started, [register a free sandbox account here](https://tcg-sandbox.shiplogic.com/register).

Once you’ve created your account and verified your email address, log in and generate an API key under **Integrations > API Keys**.

Please note that sandbox uses [https://api.shiplogic.com](https://api.shiplogic.com) instead of the URL displayed on the requests.

⚠️ When you’re ready to go live, you’ll need to register a production account with the relevant courier and create a new API key for use in the live environment.

item.name: HTTP responses
item.description:
## Response format

The The Courier Guy API returns data in application/json format. To reduce payload size and improve performance, **fields with falsy values may be omitted** from the response.

Some errors return plain text instead of JSON. To get all errors in JSON, prefix the path with "/v3", e.g. "/v3/shipments".

## Response codes

#### **200 OK**

Returned for all successful GET, PUT, PATCH, or POST requests.

#### **204 No Content**

Returned for all successful DELETE requests.

#### **400 Bad Request**

Returned when:  
• Request validation fails (e.g. a field has the wrong type or a required field is missing).  
• An invalid action is attempted (e.g. cancelling a shipment that has already been collected).

A descriptive error message is included in the response.

#### 401 Unauthorised

Returned when the user cannot be found.  
• Response message: "Error logging in".  
• Common cause: The API user has been deleted, but their API key is still in use.

#### 403 Forbidden

The user does not have permission to perform the action. A descriptive message is included.

#### 404 Not Found

Returned when an invalid endpoint is requested (e.g. [https://api.portal.thecourierguy.co.za/shipments/invalid](https://api.portal.thecourierguy.co.za/shipments/invalid)).  
Also used in rare cases where a resource cannot be found, though this is not typically expected by clients.

#### 405 Method Not Allowed

Returned when a valid endpoint is used with an invalid HTTP method (e.g. PUT on [https://api.portal.thecourierguy.co.za/shipments](https://api.portal.thecourierguy.co.za/shipments)).

#### 422 Unprocessable Entity

Returned when the server understands the request but cannot complete the action.  
Currently, this only occurs when attempting to email CSV or PDF files to an API user (API users do not have email addresses).

#### 423 Locked

Returned when requests are made with a user belonging to a closed account.

#### 429 Too Many Requests

An API user exceeds their request rate limit.

#### 500 Internal Server Error

Returned when a server-side issue occurs (e.g. database access failure).  
This error is not expected during normal operation.

### Paging

Most GET endpoints support pagination with the limit and offset query parameters.  
Note: the count property in responses is capped at 10,000 for performance reasons.

item.name: Shipment statuses
item.description:
Here’s a short description of each of the The Courier Guy shipment statuses:

**Booking, quote and payment statuses**

- **quote** – A quote has been generated but the shipment has not been booked yet.
    
- **quote-expired** – The quote is no longer valid and a new one must be requested.
    
- **payment-pending** – Awaiting payment before the shipment can be processed.
    
- **payment-failed** – Payment was unsuccessful and the shipment cannot proceed.
    
- **pending-approval** – Awaiting approval from an account owner before the shipment can be processed.
    
- **approval-rejected** – The shipment was not approved and will not be processed.
    
- **submitted** – The shipment has been booked and is awaiting collection assignment.
    
- **failed** – The shipment could not be created (e.g. validation or rating failure).
    

**Collection statuses**

- **collection-accepted** – The assigned driver has accepted the collection and is en route.
    
- **collection-assigned** – A driver has been allocated to collect the shipment.
    
- **collection-unassigned** – No driver is currently assigned for collection.
    
- **collection-rejected** – The assigned driver has rejected the collection (typically due to incorrect assignment).
    
- **collection-exception** – An unexpected issue occurred during collection (e.g. address problem).
    
- **collection-failed-attempt** – Collection was attempted but not successful.
    
- **collected** – The shipment has been successfully picked up.
    
- **awaiting-dropoff** – The shipment is waiting to be dropped off by a customer (used for lockers, kiosks and counters).
    

**Hub & transit statuses**

- **inbound-customs-and-vat** – Held at customs awaiting clearance and payment of VAT or duties (see the tracking message for details).
    
- **at-hub** – The shipment has arrived at a hub or depot.
    
- **on-hold** – The shipment is on hold pending resolution (e.g. query, instruction).
    
- **on-hold-internal** – Internal hold applied by the courier for operational reasons.
    
- **damaged** – The shipment has been damaged and cannot continue without intervention.
    
- **under-query** – The shipment is under query after leaving the freight room.
    
- **returned-to-hub** – Returned back to the hub after a failed delivery.
    
- **manifested** – The shipment has been included in an inter-hub manifest.
    
- **ready-for-dispatch** – Ready to leave the hub toward the next hub.
    
- **in-transit** – Currently in transit between hubs.
    
- **at-destination-hub** – Arrived at the hub closest to the final delivery point.
    

**Delivery statuses**

- **delivery-scheduled** – Delivery is scheduled; the shipment moves to `out-for-delivery` automatically at the scheduled time.
    
- **delivery-assigned** – A driver has been assigned for delivery.
    
- **delivery-unassigned** – Delivery driver not yet assigned.
    
- **delivery-rejected** – The assigned driver rejected the delivery (typically due to incorrect assignment).
    
- **out-for-delivery** – The shipment is with the driver on the way to the recipient.
    
- **delivery-exception** – An issue occurred during delivery (e.g. address issues).
    
- **delivery-failed-attempt** – Delivery was attempted but unsuccessful.
    
- **in-locker** – The shipment has been placed in a locker.
    
- **collect-and-return-to-hub** – The shipment is being collected from the delivery to be returned to the hub.
    
- **return-to-hub –** The shipment is on its way back to the hub.
    
- **ready-for-pickup** – The shipment is ready to be picked up by a customer (used for lockers, kiosks and counters).
    
- **delivered** – Successfully delivered to the recipient.
    

**Special statuses**

- **returned-to-sender** – Returned to the sender after failed delivery attempts.
    
- **undeliverable** – Cannot be delivered or returned (e.g. damaged, recipient unknown).
    
- **cancelled** – Shipment cancelled before completion.
    
- **floor-check** – Shipment was physically verified in the facility (floor check).
    

The following statuses aren't shown to end-users and are mapped visually to other statuses:

- **collection-unassigned** to **collection-assigned**
    
- **collection-rejected** to **collection-assigned**
    
- **delivery-unassigned** to **delivery-assigned**
    
- **delivery-rejected** to **delivery-assigned**
    
- **on-hold-internal** to **at-hub**

Third-party integrations with the "Webhook" integration type will send an entire shipment's payload when the integration is triggered. - Shipment is created

item.name: Addresses
item.description:
Addresses are central to The Courier Guy and is used for getting rates, submitting shipments etc.

The structure of an address can be seen below:

```
{
        "company": "The Courier Guy",
        "street_address": "194 Bancor Avenue",
        "type": "business",
        "local_area": "Menlyn",
        "city": "Pretoria",
        "zone": "Gauteng",
        "country": "ZA",
        "code": "0181",
        "lat": -25.7863272,
        "lng": 28.277583
}

 ```

Ideally pass through the `lat` and `lng` (latitude and longitude) for best accuracy. If the `lat` and `lng` is not passed through, The Courier Guy will attempt to geocode the address to the best of its ability. The `type` field (optional) can be `residential`, `business` , `counter` or `locker`. If no `type` is provided it will default to `unknown`.

item.name: Accounts API
Shipping and rates

request.description:
This endpoint can be used to search for pickup points close to a specific location. An alternative approach is to find pickup points within a bounding box using `min_lat`, `min_lng`, `max_lat` and `max_lng`.

In both cases the `type` parameter can optionally be used to filter the results based on the pickup point type:

- `locker`
    
- `counter`
    
- `point`

Use this endpoint to retrieve the relevant rates and service levels for a given `account_id`, `collection_address`, `delivery_address` and list of `parcels`. Optionally, include a `declared_value` (for insurance purposes), possible user `opt_in_rates` e.g. Gift wrapping and `opt_in_time_based_rates` e.g. Early-bird delivery.

See the "Getting opt-in rates" on how to get the possible `opt-in rates` and `opt-in time based` rates for a given `collection_address` and `delivery_address`. `opt_in_rates` and `opt_in_time_based_rates` should be specified as an array of ID's e.g. `"opt_in_time_based_rates":[76]`.

The following fields are required:

- `collection_address`
    
- `delivery_address`
    
- `parcels`
    

See the structure of addresses at the main section at the start of the documentation.

request.description:
The following fields are required:

- `collection_address`
    
- `collection_contact`
    
- `delivery_address`
    
- `delivery_contact`
    
- `parcels`
    
- either `service_level_code` or `service_level_id` (returned when retrieving rates)
    

See the structure of addresses at the main section at the start of the documentation.

The `collection_contact` and `delivery_contact` requires at least an `email`and/or `mobile_number`.

`mute_notifications`: If this property is set to `true`, no SMS and/or email notifications will be sent on behalf of this shipment.

`customer_reference`: Any reference you want to add to the shipment e.g. an order number or external ID you want to associate with the shipment.

`customer_reference_name`: This optional field describes what the customer reference refers to e.g. `PO number`, `Order no.`, `Internal ref`, etc.

Optionally, include a `declared_value` (for insurance purposes), possible user `opt_in_rates` e.g. Gift wrapping and `opt_in_time_based_rates` e.g. Early-bird delivery.

See the "Getting opt-in rates" on how to get the possible `opt-in rates` and `opt-in time based` rates for a given `collection_address` and `delivery_address`. `opt_in_rates` and `opt_in_time_based_rates` should be specified as an array of ID's e.g. `"opt_in_time_based_rates":[76]`.

The `collection_min_date` and `delivery_min_date` can be used if you'd like the collection or delivery to take place only at a later stage. You can also send ⁠ `enforce_strict_delivery_times` ⁠ as ⁠`true` to the endpoint to ensure that `⁠ delivery_after` ⁠ and ⁠ `delivery_before` ⁠ is adhered to. This is for special cases only e.g. liquor deliveries, so first discuss it with the courier before implementing it.

`due_date` is a field used for reporting purposes. It doesn't change anything operationally.

On a parcel, set an optional `alternative_tracking_reference` if you have preprinted tracking stickers or a pre-defined barcode that will be linked to the parcel.

# Error messages

Below is a list of error responses that the shipment-creation endpoint can return.

### General errors

- **`do not specify a shipment ID when creating a new shipment`** — request  
    body contains a non-zero `id`.
    
- **`failed to fill shipment pickup point provider`** — invalid combination of  
    pickup-point identifiers.
    

### For returns (`is_return: true`)

- **`failed to get shipment`** — no shipment found with the supplied  
    `short_tracking_reference` to return from.
    
- **`shipment with the tracking reference {ref} already exists`** — a return  
    for this reference has already been created.
    

### Tracking references

- **`you may not set a custom tracking reference for a shipment`**
    
- **`cannot set custom reference — value exceeds maximum character limit of {n}`**
    
- **`custom tracking reference should be more than {n} characters`**
    
- **`custom tracking reference should not be more than {n} characters`**
    
- **`custom tracking reference should only contain alphanumeric values and dashes`**
    
- **`shipment with the custom tracking reference {ref} already exists`**
    
- **`invalid custom tracking reference prefix`** — value does not match any of  
    the allowed prefixes configured for the account.
    

### Customer reference

- **`customer reference should not be less than {n} characters`**
    
- **`customer reference should not be more than {n} characters`**
    

### Parcel references / aliases

- **`there are multiple parcels with the same reference`**
    
- **`parcel alternative tracking reference needs to be greater than {n} characters`**
    
- **`custom tracking reference should not be more than {n} characters`**
    
- **`alternative tracking reference is not unique for parcel: {value}`**
    
- **`customer alias needs to be greater than {n} characters`**
    
- **`customer alias should not be more than {n} characters`**
    
- **`customer alias is not unique for parcel: {value}`**
    
- **`parcel alternative tracking reference already exists`**
    

### Dates / time windows

- **`due date cannot be in the past`**
    
- **`invalid collection_after`** — value could not be parsed as a time string.
    
- **`invalid collection_before`**
    
- **`invalid delivery_after`**
    
- **`invalid delivery_before`**
    
- **`rate has expired – please try again`** — selected `service_level_id`  
    belongs to a rate revision that has expired (>5 min ago).
    

### Addresses / contacts

- **`collection postal_code is required`** — provider requires postal codes  
    on creation.
    
- **`delivery postal_code is required`** — same as above.
    
- **`could not create shipment: collection_address missing`**
    
- **`could not create shipment: collection_contact missing`**
    
- **`could not create shipment: collection_contact needs a valid email or mobile_number`**
    
- **`could not create shipment: delivery_address missing`**
    
- **`could not create shipment: delivery_contact missing`**
    
- **`could not create shipment: delivery_contact needs a valid email or mobile_number`**
    
- **`invalid collection contact mobile number`**
    
- **`invalid delivery contact mobile number`**
    
- **`invalid responsible contact mobile number`**
    
- **`name should be less than 255 characters`**
    
- **`mobile number should be less than 255 characters`**
    
- **`alternative contact number should be less than 255 characters`**
    
- **`email should be less than 255 characters`**
    
- **`the collection address and delivery address shouldn't be the same address`**
    

### Parcels

- **`could not create shipment: parcels missing`**
    
- **`parcel exceeds the maximum weight of {n} kg`**
    
- **`the parcel's dimensions exceed the maximum allowable size of {l} cm x {w} cm x {h} cm`**
    
- **`parcel length is empty`** (only when a weight is also missing)
    
- **`parcel width is empty`**
    
- **`parcel height is empty`**
    
- **`Pickup point shipments can only have one parcel`**
    

### Insurance / declared value

- **`cannot set declared value: Provider does not have liability cover enabled`**
    
- **`declared value is more than the allowed maximum ({max})`**
    

### Status / POD method

- **`{value} is not a valid status`** — for either `shipment.status` or any  
    `parcel.status`.
    
- **`invalid value for proof of delivery method`** — `pod_method` not in the  
    allowed list.
    

### Cost centres

- **`invalid cost centre ID`** — ID supplied without an account, or ID does  
    not belong to the supplied account.
    
- **`invalid cost centre name`** — name supplied without an account, or no  
    cost centre by that name exists for the account.
    

### Account state

- **`this account is closed`** — the supplied `account_id` has  
    `status = closed`.
    
- **`could not get current account`** — account lookup failed.
    
- **`could not create shipment: failed to get account information - {err}`**
    
- **`the credit limit for the account has been reached`** — post-paid account  
    whose new balance would exceed its credit limit.
    
- **`insufficient funds for the account`** — prepaid account with too low a  
    balance.
    

### Guest shipments

- **`this feature is disabled. Please contact support`** — guest shipment  
    creation is disabled.
    
- **`An error occurred while creating the shipment. Please contact support for assistance.`**
    

### Rates

- **`there are no rates for the specified service level, declared value and addresses`** .
    
- **`no service levels available for the declared value`** — declared value  
    exceeds liability cover for every service level.
    
- **`no service levels available`** — no service levels matched the request.
    
- **`could not find rates for the requested service level code`**
    

### Database constraint surfacing

- **`... already exists`** (generic) — any DB error containing  
    `"already exists"` is surfaced as `400` rather than `500`.
    

---

## 403 Forbidden

- **`you cannot create a return for a shipment that is not delivered yet.`** —  
    account members attempting to return a non-delivered shipment.
    

---

## 412 Precondition Failed

- **`customer reference is required`** — the collection or destination branch  
    requires a customer reference and none was supplied.
    
- **`customer reference is required: {prefix}`** — same as above, but the  
    branch has a required prefix that the caller must use.
    

---

## 500 Internal Server Error

Returned when an unexpected server-side failure occurs. These are not caused  
by the caller and generally indicate the request should be retried later or  
escalated to support.

- **`failed to check account approval setting`**
    
- **`failed to get provider settings`** — settings lookup failed.
    
- **`could not select all shipment fields`**
    
- **`could not update parcel statuses`**
    
- **`failed to delete shipment`**, **`failed to delete tracking events for shipment`**, **`failed to reverse shipment charge`**
    
- **`could not check if cost centres are enabled`**
    
- **`could not create shipment`**

Use this endpoint to get signed URLs to POD images. POD file names can be found in tracking events. See the `Tracking a shipment` GET request for more information.

Please note that the `file_name` parameter is an array of filenames and `folder` has a constant value of `shipment-images`

This endpoint takes a tracking reference as a query parameter and return the shipment's status, together with an array of tracking events for that shipment.

On each event there is a property called `parcel_id`. If the `parcel_id` is 0, the event refers to the shipment status. If the `parcel_id` > 0, the status refers to the appropriate parcel of the shipment.

Please use this endpoint responsibly: Only when needed and only if you’re authorised to access the information.

## PODs

If a shipment is delivered, a POD can be provided in a few ways. The `message` property of the `tracking_event` can be used to determine the POD method used:

- `POD image captured`
    
- `Recipient details entered`
    
- `PIN entered successfully`
    

If the message is `POD image captured`, the actual POD images can be found within the `data` property with the following structure:

```
"tracking_events": [
  {
    "id": 332,
    "parcel_id": 0,
    data: {
        type: "proof-of-delivery-images",
        images: ["442-aff78c7a-b08a-45c7-b46d-67e3fae607fa.jpg"],
        pdfs: ["233-bef78c7a-ag43-45c7-b46d-67e3fae607fa.pdf"]
      },
    ...
  }
]

 ```

The POD can either be a set of images and/or PDFs. The files are stored on S3 and requires a signed S3 URL. See the `POD image downloads` section.

item.name: Get signed URL to upload a file

request.description:
Returns a pre-signed S3 URL that can be used to upload a file directly to S3. This must be called before adding a file (image or PDF) to a shipment, since the new POD endpoint accepts file references (filenames/UUIDs) rather than embedded file data.

**Query parameters:**

- `file_name`: The filename or UUID-based name for the file to be uploaded (e.g. `48841aa7-2a58-4053-b902-5aaaaeac1722.png`)
    
- `folder`: The S3 folder/bucket path to upload into. Use `shipment-images` for POD images or `shipment-pdfs` for PDFs.
    
- `mime_type`: The MIME type of the file (e.g. `image/png`, `application/pdf`)
    

**Workflow:**

1. Call this endpoint to get a pre-signed upload URL.
    
2. Use the returned URL to PUT the file directly to S3.
    
3. Pass the `file_name` value in the `images` or `pdfs` array when calling the POD endpoint.

request.description:
This endpoint captures a POD for a shipment and marks the shipment as "delivered" if it is not yet delivered.

There are various mutations of the body of the request:

1. `shipment_ids` is an array of shipment IDs to capture the POD for. Alternatively, `tracking_reference` can be used to identify the shipment.
    
2. `parcel_id` identifies the specific parcel within the shipment (use `0` if not applicable).
    
3. `date` is the timestamp of when the POD occurred. If left out, it will default to `now()`.
    
4. `message` should define how the POD was captured. The options are:
    - "Recipient details entered"
        
    - "POD file(s) captured"
        
    - "Recipient details entered and POD file(s) captured"
        
5. `images` is an array of image file reference strings (filenames/UUIDs) that have already been uploaded to S3 separately — files are **not** embedded in this request.
    
6. `pdfs` is an array of PDF file reference strings that have already been uploaded to S3 separately — files are **not** embedded in this request.
    
7. `metadata` is an optional object containing recipient details:
    
    - `name_and_surname`: Full name of the recipient
        
    - `mobile_number`: Recipient's mobile number
        
    - `department`: Department or location where the POD was captured
        
    - `description`: Additional description or notes
        
    - `id_number`: Recipient's ID number
        

**Workflow:**

1. Call "Get signed URL to upload a file" (`GET /s3-url/upload`) to get a pre-signed S3 URL for each file.
    
2. PUT the file directly to S3 using the returned URL.
    
3. Pass the `file_name` value(s) in the `images` or `pdfs` array in this request.

item.name: Link parcels to the load unit

request.description:
Links one parcel to a load unit. Call it once per parcel as it is packed - this is the scan action at the packing station.

Identify the load unit with `load_unit_id`, or with `reference` (either the system or the alternative reference) so a scanner can post exactly what it read. Identify the parcel with `parcel_reference`, which accepts either the parcel tracking reference or its alternative tracking reference.

Each successful link is recorded as a `parcel-added-to-load-unit` system event on the parcel's shipment, so the shipment's event trail shows which container it travelled in.

item.name: Get parcels on a load unit

item.description:
A load unit is a physical container - a cage, pallet, bag or consolidated box - that groups parcels together so they can be moved and scanned as one. Instead of scanning fifty parcels onto a manifest one at a time, you scan the load unit once.

Every load unit has a **system reference** that we generate for you (e.g. \`CAGE-CB\`). It is short, uses an ambiguity-free character set (no vowels, no \`0\`/\`O\` or \`1\`/\`I\`/\`L\`) and is unique. You can also set your own **alternative_reference**, which is what your operators see on screen when it is set. Either reference identifies the load unit everywhere in the API.

Load unit references share a namespace with shipment and parcel references - a reference can never be both - so a scanner can post whatever was scanned without knowing which kind of thing it is.

Typical flow:
1. Create the load unit (`POST /load-units`) and print its barcode (`GET /load-units/barcode`) if needed.
2. Link parcels to it as they are packed (`POST /load-units/parcels`).
3. When it ships, add its parcels to a manifest (`POST /interhub-transfers/parcels`).
4. Empty it when it is unpacked (`DELETE /load-units/parcels` with `clear_all`).

A load unit is long-lived - the same physical cage is emptied and refilled - so clear its parcels rather than deleting it.
